headline: South Asia: Pakistan urges Gulf de-escalation as US, Iran trade accusations at UN
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistan urges Gulf de-escalation as US, Iran trade accusations at UN.
- Persian Gulf Region: Trump tells advisers he may hold off on Iran attacks barring new provocations.
- Asia: Musk ordered to preserve records on Ukraine’s Starlink access by Democratic US senators.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Navy unveils special warfare-themed uniforms for upcoming Army-Navy game.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Navy unveils special warfare-themed uniforms for upcoming Army-Navy game.
The U.S. Navy released images of Navy Midshipmen uniforms for the 2026 Army-Navy game that honor the service's Naval special warfare components.
- Military Times, one day ago: US Air Force adopts new Force Design focusing on sensors and autonomy.
The Air Force's new Force Design 2026 outlines a shift toward artificial intelligence, autonomy and integrated sensors to counter emerging threats.
The Caribbean - bottom line: 2027 Rhodes Scholar hopes to transform healthcare through tech.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: 2027 Rhodes Scholar hopes to transform healthcare through tech.
For Somesh Sharma, being named Jamaica’s 2027 Rhodes Scholar is more than a dream fulfilled. It is a chance to turn opportunity into lasting impact and give back to the country that shaped him. “I am feeling very happy, elated. [I] can’t believe it. I’m very thankful to receive this award. it’s been an incredible journey,” the 22-year-old said after the announcement was made on Thursday at King’s House in St Andrew.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE

- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Russian drone strike kills man on scooter in Zaporizhzhia Oblast.
A 45-year-old civilian riding along the central road of Kushuhum has been killed in a Russian drone attack.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Two killed and one injured in Russian strike on infrastructure facility in Chernihiv Oblast.
Two men have been killed and another has sustained injuries as a result of a Russian attack on a critical infrastructure facility in the town of Mena, Chernihiv Oblast.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russian drone attack sparks large fire at Naftogaz facility in Poltava Oblast.
A Russian drone strike caused a major fire at a Naftogaz Group facility in central Ukraine on Saturday afternoon. Staff were safe in shelters.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Police officer shields injured boy, 9, during repeat Russian attack in Sumy Oblast.
Police officers in Sumy Oblast have rescued a 54-year-old woman and her nine-year-old grandson after a Russian attack caused a fire at their home. When Russian forces attempted a second drone strike, one of the officers shielded the boy with his body.
Southern Europe - bottom line: EU, UK ‘Concerned’ as Kosovo Moves Against Hague Court’s Powers Again.
- Balkan Insight, one day ago: EU, UK ‘Concerned’ as Kosovo Moves Against Hague Court’s Powers Again.
The EU and the UK warn Kosovo MPs not to pass an amended law curbing the powers of the Hague-based Kosovo Specialist Chambers war crimes court without consultations with international allies.

Trump has alternated between threats of escalating the war with new strikes and winding down hostilities, and current and former officials say he does not appear to have made up his mind.

Netanyahu called for a national unity government following his meeting with Eisenkot, invoking the Hatikvah walkout and warning of Iran's nuclear threat.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 7 hours ago: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting at APEC: What to expect.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan urges Gulf de-escalation as US, Iran trade accusations at UN.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 14 hours ago: Pakistan urges Gulf de-escalation as US, Iran trade accusations at UN.
UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan on Friday called for an immediate end to military provocations in the Gulf and renewed regional diplomacy as the United States, Iran and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries exchanged sharply conflicting accusations at a UN Security Council meeting on attacks against shipping and threats to maritime security. The debate highlighted growing concerns that the confrontation could disrupt international trade, energy supplies and food shipments while increasing the risk of a wider regional conflict.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Pakistan, 16 other countries, condemn Israeli strike on southern Gaza hospital.
Pakistan and 16 other countries,on Saturday condemned the Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, calling on Tel Aviv to protect civilians and medical facilities and ensure the sustained and unimpeded delivery of humanitarian aid to the Palestinian enclave. The deadliest single strike since Israel’s elections last month hit the surgery ward of Nasser Hospital in Khan Yunis early on Thursday, killing at least six Palestinians, including a 13-year-old boy, and wounding nearly 30 others.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Major among 4 troops martyred, 24 terrorists killed during operations in KP and Balochistan: ISPR.
Four troops, including a major, were martyred while 24 terrorists were killed in multiple intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan, the military’s media wing said on Saturday. In a statement, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that since Nov 13, armed forces have been conducting multiple IBOs “around Kolpur, Kardagap and Nushki, including area domination and patrolling of the Quetta-Taftan National Highway (N-40) to keep it secure for local traffic and sustain operations”.
- The Hindu - International, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Myanmar airstrike on displaced persons camp kills 12, say witnesses.

Democratic US senators have told Elon Musk to preserve all records related to his company SpaceX’s restrictions on Ukraine’s use of its Starlink and Starshield satellite services. Ukrainian forces say Starshield, the military-grade version of ‌Starlink, is vital for frontline communications and drone operations in their defence against Russian drone and missile attacks. - South China Morning Post - China, 15 hours ago: Cleaner, smarter, big data: the PLA’s bet on ‘sunshine’ military recruitment.
The Chinese military is mining big data to get better recruits and stamp out corruption in the march towards its centenary next year. As part of an overhaul called “end-to-end sunshine” recruitment, the People’s Liberation Army has been commanded to use data-driven systems across the the enlistment process to build a military “focused on war readiness”. The orders came this month from the general offices of the Central Military Commission and State Council and mark a renewed push to eradicate...
- South China Morning Post - China, 9 hours ago: How Chinese custom ‘chong xi,’ or ‘clashing with joy,’ can counteract misfortune.
In ancient China, when a man became seriously ill, his family might arrange a wedding for him in an attempt to drive away the disease. The custom is called chong xi, literally translated as “clashing with joy”. Its rationale is that a happy event could lift one’s spirits and thereby dispel illness or other misfortunes. - Times of India - Top Stories, 8 hours ago: Dragged, beaten with sticks, fists: J'khand woman killed over Rs 500 owed by dead man.

Following an altercation, Bankira was attacked by the accused, leading to her death from severe injuries. Evidence collected during the investigation included blood-stained items linked to the crime.

The arrested men have been identified as Vikas Thakur (alias Vicky), a resident of Punjab's Jalandhar, and Deep (alias Deepak Singh). Deepak was wanted in the shooting and murder of Punjab-based influencer Mad Sandhu in Amritsar on October 3.

Experts say disruption exposes ‘Australia’s reliance on foreign technology’ as software giant says services being restored Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The Microsoft outage could be a disaster for the Australian economy that forces some small businesses to close, with costs expected to run into the billions of dollars, experts have warned. The US software company has said it is “deeply sorry” for a widespread outage that caused disruption to millions of users, organisations and businesses across the globe – and that it has “addressed the underlying issue”.
